value.name: witness testifies about abusive marriage
value.description: A woman on the witness stand says she was her husband's sexual slave for thirty-six years, with a brief exception while he was in the Navy in Korea.
evidence: LAWYER Mrs. Guttman, you have testified that you were your husband's sexual slave for thirty-six years, ever since you were married --
WITNESS Except for two years when he was in the Navy, in Korea.

value.name: witness reveals former job
value.description: Mrs. Guttman says that before marriage she worked as a hostess for Trans-World Airlines.
evidence: LAWYER Prior to your marriage, what was your profession?
WITNESS I was a hostess. For Trans-World Airlines.

value.name: witness describes husband's successful business
value.description: Mrs. Guttman identifies her husband as a successful manufacturer of staples and industrial brad-tacks.
evidence: LAWYER What is your husband's profession?
WITNESS He manufactures staples and industrial brad-tacks. He's very successful.

value.name: Miles and Wrigley discuss case evidence
value.description: At counsel table, Miles quietly tells Wrigley that the opposing side has video evidence and nothing else.
evidence: At the counsel's table in the foreground Miles chats, voice lowered with WRIGLEY, a boyish, bespectacled junior associate.

WRIGLEY Wait... He wants to give her...?
MILES Nothing.
WRIGLEY And she has...?
MILES Video.

value.name: Miles rebukes Wrigley
value.description: Miles reacts with indignation to Wrigley's reaction and scolds him for speaking out of turn.
evidence: Miles turns to Wrigley with a look of indignation.

value.name: Miles questions mentoring choice
value.description: Miles tells Wrigley he doubts him as a mentee and jokes that he might have been better off mentoring someone else.
evidence: MILES Sometimes I have serious doubts about you.
MILES Am I mentoring the wrong mentee?
MILES I could be mentoring Kramer. Kramer clerked for Scalia.

value.name: Wrigley is shaken by Miles's criticism
value.description: Wrigley becomes visibly demoralized after Miles compares him unfavorably to Kramer.

value.name: lawyer asks victim to leave abusive relationship
value.description: A background lawyer asks whether the woman could simply have walked away from the abusive marriage.
evidence: BACKGROUND LAWYER (O.S.) Couldn't you simply walk away from this abusive relationship?

value.name: witness cites videotape as coercion
value.description: Mrs. Guttman answers that she could not leave because her husband had videos.
evidence: WOMAN No, he had the videos...
